summary: Share registry validation and commit-graph ancestry across tickets in one activity batch

delivery.outcome: Ticket activity resolution inside one ActivityReadBatch validates the receipt registry once and answers ancestry inside the target history from one commit-graph read, so the worktree overlap checker finishes within the wellman check budget on large adopters with unchanged results.
nonGoals: No change to standalone (unbatched) resolution, activity policy, receipt schema or terminal-outcome rules.
No weakening of batch exit revalidation; every observed relation is still re-answered from fresh Git state.
No change to worktree pair comparison or the 480 s wellman budget.

architecture.decision: Batch-scoped memoization only: the validated registry is cached under its exact text and repositoryRef; from the second ancestry probe on a full commit ID a topological rev-list graph answers questions whose newer commit is inside it (absent older or unreadable newer is False, as merge-base). Non-SHA operands and commits outside every graph keep merge-base. Exit revalidation re-reads each graph root once. Source and bundled projection stay byte-identical and ship in one immutable release.
architecture.rollback: Revert to accepted base 6738f734d7f19e178996c671c26e4165e8b21d4a; the previous immutable release remains available.

validation.evidence: Batched equals standalone with distinct terminals, an unintegrated head and an off-target terminal; one registry validation per batch (40 before).
Graph ancestry equals merge-base on every pair of a merge and criss-cross history, unknown and unreadable commits included.
283 -> 28 subprocesses for 40 distinct-terminal receipts; heyasa overlap checker 216 s -> 77 s with identical passing report.
Existing invalidation tests still fail closed; hub gate and pull-request scope gate pass.
